page: Microsoft Azure L32aos_v4 is a storage-optimized virtual machine provisioned via Microsoft Hyper-V. The instance is powered by an x86_64 AMD EPYC 9V74 processor operating at 3.7 GHz, delivering 32 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 16 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading enabled. The CPU includes 32 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache, backed by vector and cryptographic extensions including AVX-512, VAES, and SHA-NI.

Hardware capacity features 256.0 GB of system memory, providing an 8.0 GB per-vCPU ratio. Storage provisioned on the host includes 23,038 GB of bundled local NVMe SSD, delivering high-density ephemeral disk capacity. The configuration includes no discrete graphics processing units and zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong single-core and cryptographic execution, with stress-ng single-core reaching 3,077.95 and Geekbench single-core scoring 2,085.0. Multi-core performance is solid, evidenced by a Geekbench multi-core score of 17,812.0 and PassMark encryption performance of 38,579.19. Memory throughput registered 73.38 GB/sec for uncached 256MB reads and 55.9 GB/sec for writes. In application benchmarks, Redis achieved 46.17 million SET operations per second, while static web serving reached 30.26 GB/sec.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the instance aggregates massive local NVMe disk volume and substantial RAM per compute unit, lowering operational overhead for I/O-intensive workloads compared to provisioning external block storage. However, ephemeral local storage necessitates application-level data redundancy. The server is suited for high-throughput relational and NoSQL databases, transactional indexing, distributed file stores, and big data search clusters.
description: Microsoft Azure L32aos_v4 is a storage-optimized cloud virtual machine featuring 32 dedicated vCPUs and 16 physical cores running on an AMD EPYC 9V74 processor at 3.7 GHz. Equipped with 256.0 GB of RAM, it maintains an allocation of 8.0 GB per vCPU alongside 23,038 GB of high-speed local NVMe SSD storage. The x86_64 architecture incorporates AVX-512 and cryptographic accelerators, showing strong single-thread execution in Geekbench (2,085.0) and PassMark encryption benchmarks, combined with robust multi-core Geekbench metrics (17,812.0). Bundling massive NVMe disk space directly onto the host provides significant economic and throughput advantages over detached storage volumes, though reliance on local disks requires upstream resilience strategies. L32aos_v4 is well structured for I/O-intensive workloads, including distributed NoSQL databases, large-scale search engines, transactional processing systems, and data indexing pipelines.
